notes.text: I'm deciding to treat all 38 rows as active channels, ignoring the "not patched" comments as instructed. Then I'm organizing categories in order: drums, bass, guitars, keyboards, strings/brass, vocals, tracks, speakers, and other remaining items.
For the drum kit, I'm working out the specific sub-order: kick, snare, hihat, rack toms, floor tom, overheads, then percussion — with Tom1-3 as rack toms and Tom4 as the floor tom.

The overheads OH L and OH R stay as separate mono channels rather than a stereo pair, following the naming convention rule. Then percussion follows in list order (Pads, PERC1, PERC2), giving the full drum sequence.

Moving to bass (BassDI, BassMic), then guitars — checking EG1/EG2 and the acoustic pair for any L/R stereo naming, finding none, so each stays mono in given order. Keys follow next with Keys1 and Keys2.

For horns and strings, since the convention doesn't dictate an order between the two groups, I'll just preserve the input order: Horns 1, Horns 2, Strings 1, Strings 2. Vocals follow as VOX1 through VOX5, then the track stems in their given sequence, and finally HOST for speech.

Since no sockets were specified for any row, I'm patching in channel order: non-track channels go to local inputs 1-24 first, overflowing to AES50-A starting from 1, while all track channels get routed to USB per the instructions instead. Counting it out, non-track channels total 30 (12 drums, 2 bass, 4 guitars, 2 keys, 2 horns, 2 strings, 5 vocals, 1 speech), so the first 24 land on LCL 1-24 and…

Gain and head-amp settings (20dB gain, 0dB trim) only apply to the LCL/A/B/C socketed channels since those have physical head amps, while the USB-routed track channels don't get head-amp settings since USB has no head amp. I need to number channels in the order they're written across the whole desk, applying the LCL-then-AES50-A patch counting only to the non-track channels as they appear sequent…

I'm laying out the full 38-channel order (Kick through Click/Guide) and mapping the first 24 non-track channels to LCL sockets 1-24, with the remaining VOX/HOST channels overflowing onto the AES50 A bank starting at channel 25.

For the track group (31-38), I'm routing those to USB sockets 1-8 as instructed. Then I'm moving into per-category processing settings — starting with drums (HPF 40Hz, red color, DCA Drums, included in the Band mute group) and bass (HPF 80Hz, since it counts as a band instrument alongside drums, guitars, and vocals).

Now working through the rest: guitars and keys get 80Hz HPF, horns get 100Hz, strings get 80Hz as general band instruments, and both vocals and speech get 120Hz HPF. Tracks themselves skip HPF, the Band mute group, and the INST Reverb send entirely.
Color coding assigns Drums-Red, Bass-Blue, Guitars-Magenta, Keyboards-Cyan, Strings/Brass-Orange, Vocals-Green, Tracks/Playback-Yellow, and Speech-Purple.

For DCAs, since Bass isn't given its own dedicated group in the named list (Drums, Guitars, Keys, Vocals, Tracks, Strings, Horns, Band, Speech), it falls under the Band DCA per the instruction to include anything not otherwise assigned.

Now for mute groups, I'm organizing Band (drums, bass, guitars, keys, strings, horns), Vocals, Speech (HOST), and FX (busses) separately, noting that tracks are excluded from the Band mute group per the instructions. Moving to bus setup, I'm working through monitor busses first, then mix, then FX — MON1-MON4 as mono busses routed to dedicated local XLR outputs 1-4 rather than the main mix.

For sends, every channel except speech routes to every monitor bus pre-fader, with level set all the way down at -144 dB but left unmuted since they're still technically active sends. I'm figuring out how to express "every channel except HOST" in the from-list format, likely by explicitly listing all channel names except speech.

Now I'm sketching out the mix busses: a Drums bus combining all twelve drum channels feeding Main, a Drums Comp duplicate that's heavily compressed and pulled down -6dB also feeding Main, a Vocals bus grouping VOX1-5 (excluding HOST speech since it's not categorized as a vocal) feeding Main, and a Keys bus since there are two keyboard channels justifying its own group.

I'm also creating Horns and Strings busses since each has two channels, then laying out FX sends: VOX Reverb and VOX Delay covering all vocal channels post-unity, a Snare Verb send at -10dB pre, and an INST Reverb bus covering non-drum instruments like bass, guitars, keys, horns, and strings at -144dB post. Now I'm moving on to configuring the main channel.

Since Drums Comp shares the same channels as the Drums bus, those channels stay excluded from a direct main route. That leaves Bass and Guitars as clear non-bus channels heading to main, while track channels need closer inspection—click and guide are monitor-only for musicians, but other track channels like T DRUMS or T Bass represent part of the band's sound and should route to main.

I'm treating HOST as a regular speech channel that isn't part of the band, so it gets a normal direct route to main. So overall, drums, vocals, keys, horns, and strings channels have no direct main route since they're fully handled through their mix buses, while Bass, Guitars, most Tracks, and HOST route directly to main—except Click/Guide tracks, which stay monitor-only.

For monitor sends, only speech is excluded, so every other channel including Click/Guide feeds the monitor busses as expected. Now I'm setting up the FX DCA assignment across the VOX Reverb, VOX Delay, Snare Verb, and INST Reverb busses, along with matching mute groups, before moving into channel processing specifics like HPF settings, phantom power, and gain/trim values for the drum channels.

Continuing through the input list, I'm applying 80Hz highpass to the bass DI, bass mic, both electric guitars, and both acoustic guitars, with standard 20dB gain and zero trim, while keeping the 40Hz highpass and gain settings consistent across toms, overheads, pads, and percussion.

Keys and strings get an 80Hz highpass, horns get 100Hz, and vocals plus the host mic get 120Hz. The USB track inputs skip gain and phantom power since there's no head-amp, but they still get trim set to 0 per the convention that trim applies to every channel. For faders, since the instruction says to leave them all the way down, I'm setting fader_db to -144 across the board.

Since muting wasn't explicitly stated, I'll leave that field null rather than assume. Monitor buses also go all the way down to -144, while mix buses sit at unity 0.0 except Drums Comp which gets -6dB, and FX buses stay at unity as well. DCA faders weren't specified so I'm skipping those.

Now I'm working through the channel groupings for each bus's sends — listing out Drums (Kick, Snare, HiHat, the toms, overheads, Pads, and percussion), Vocals (VOX 1 through 5), and starting on Keys and Horns bus channel lists.

I'm also mapping out the instrument reverb bus, which pulls in Bass, Guitars, Keys, Horns, and Strings channels but excludes drums, vocals, and speech — totaling 12 channels. Separately, vocal reverb/delay covers all five VOX channels, and there's a dedicated Snare reverb send set to -10dB pre-fader. For main routing, I'm setting up the convention where Main only routes through Matrix1 with no di…

So Main's routing to Matrix1 should actually be captured in Matrix1's fed_by field pointing back to the main bus, rather than as a separate output entry for Main itself, since Main has no physical output of its own but the output schema still requires a patch field for actual outputs.

I'm mapping out the channel list with patch groups: channels 1-24 use sequential LCL sockets, 25-30 (VOX1-5, HOST) use sequential A sockets, and track channels get the USB patch group. I'll just specify the group name and let the numbering fall out automatically rather than hardcoding socket numbers, since overflow beyond 24 doesn't need explicit sockets either.

No stereo pairs are needed beyond the OH L/R which stays mono. For mute groups, I'm organizing Band (drums, bass, guitars, keys, horns, strings) separately from Vocals (VOX1-5) and Speech (HOST), plus an FX group for the FX busses, and figuring out what falls under the general Band DCA versus dedicated ones.
Also adding FX mute group for the reverb/delay busses, then mapping out the remaining DCA assignments: Drums, Guitars, Keys, Vocals, Tracks, Strings, Horns, and Band (bass channels).

For the gain structure, I'm setting trim_db to 0 across every channel including tracks, while gain_db of 20 only applies to non-track channels with head-amps. Send modes are already settled -- pre for monitors, post for mix and FX -- so nothing more needed there before I compile everything into the final JSON output.

I'm checking that tracks route correctly to USB, HPF stays null per convention, and channel gains are set properly — noting the BassDI gain of 20dB makes sense since DI channels typically carry gain unlike USB inputs.

Now I'm verifying that all the drum channels marked "not patched" in the input should still be treated as normal patched channels per instructions, confirming Snare Verb sends only apply to Snare, INST Reverb sends are set fully down post-fader, and Track channels are properly excluded from HPF, band mute groups, and INST Reverb. I'm also confirming vocal channels get VOX Reverb/Delay, HOST corre…

Since there's no dedicated Bass DCA defined by convention, I'm confirming Bass channels correctly fall into the Band DCA, and that Guitars DCA exists as expected. I'm verifying all instrumental channels (guitars, keys, horns, strings, bass, drums) properly receive the Band mute group, that Drums DCA correctly includes percussion channels like Pads and PERC, and that phantom power and patching not…

Counting all input rows against the plan's 38 channels confirms nothing was missed, so I'm now checking whether the channel order follows the stated convention of drums, bass, guitars, keyboards, strings/brass, vocals, tracks, then speakers - starting to verify the plan's actual ordering against this sequence.

Comparing the plan's layout to that convention, I notice HOST (speech/speaker feed) is placed at position 30, right before tracks (31-38), which contradicts the rule that tracks should precede speakers. This looks like a genuine ordering violation worth flagging, especially since instructions.md doesn't override the convention here.
Checking the horns/strings sequence, the convention groups "strings or brass" together without specifying internal order, so that part is fine either way.

Now I'm verifying the patch assignment: VOX1 correctly starts at AES50-A since the first 24 LCL sockets are already consumed by drums through strings, so the next available bank logically begins there.

Tracking further, HOST at AES50-A6 lines up correctly after VOX1-VOX5 occupy A1-5, and tracks are patched to USB 1-8 per the given override instructions, so those pieces are consistent. The real issue remains the ordering violation - HOST should follow tracks, not precede them, per the stated convention. I'm now moving to check the bus ordering convention, which specifies monitor busses first, th…

Checking the mono/stereo fields, MON1-4 correctly marked mono:true per the "MONO busses" convention, mix busses (Drums, Drums Comp, Vocals, Keys, Horns, Strings) correctly marked stereo, and the FX busses (VOX Reverb, VOX Delay, Snare Verb, INST Reverb) also correctly marked stereo since the text explicitly states so - no unnecessary "inferred" tags needed there since the source text stated it di…

Now examining Main/Matrix indexes - Main1 inferred since there's only one Main in the plan, Matrix1 inferred from its slot name, both reasonable. The Drums Comp bus omits compressor parameters since this format has no field for them, which is an honest omission note.

Checking DCA and mute group assignments for FX - both correctly include all four FX return busses (VOX Reverb, VOX Delay, Snare Verb, INST Reverb), matching the stated convention that FX should include all effects return busses.

For DCA "Band," the convention says it should catch anything not in a named DCA group, so Bass correctly falls there since it isn't a named category. The mute group "Band" similarly applies to drums, bass, guitars, keys, horns, and strings, while properly excluding vocals, speech, and tracks channels - and I'm confirming Tracks channels end up with no mute group assigned at all.

I'm now cross-checking HPF values: drums at 40Hz, and 80Hz applied across bass, guitars, keys, and strings as generic band instruments, with horns overridden to 100Hz and vocals/speech to 120Hz per the specific rules - everything lines up correctly with no unwarranted overrides.

Color mapping checks out too: both strings and horns are correctly colored orange per "Strings/Brass-Orange." I confirm the BassDI gain of 20dB is fine for a DI input, the HOST speech channel correctly has no monitor sends or reverb since it's not a vocal or instrument track, and the HOST DCA is properly labeled "Speech."

Moving on, the mute group for HOST is correctly "Speech," and the Tracks DCA assignment is also correct. Click/Guide correctly has empty main_routes since click tracks shouldn't hit the main mix, while other track channels correctly default to being routed to Main since the exclusion rule only applies to click/guide specifically. BassDI and BassMic routing also checks out as not included in the m…

Guitars, keys, horns, and strings look right too - since there's no defined Guitars bus convention (only rules for multiple keyboards, horns, or strings), guitars correctly route straight to main without a bus assignment, while keys correctly route through the Keys bus with empty main_routes since the bus already feeds main. Vocals follow the same pattern with empty main_routes since the Vocals b…

Drums check out similarly, with empty main_routes since the Drums bus feeds main directly, and Bass channels correctly stay routed direct to main since there's no dedicated Bass mix bus. The DCA groupings for Guitars and Keys both look properly defined with valid members. So the main issue I've found remains the ordering violation with speech appearing before tracks - now I want to verify the dru…

Checking the tom sequence, Tom1-3 are rack toms followed by Tom4 as the floor tom, then overheads, then percussion elements like Pads and PERC1/2 - this matches the convention correctly. Pads being categorized as drums despite being an Instrument type also fits within the "other percussion" catch-all at the end of the ordering.

The main flaw remains speech tracks appearing before the drum group violates the intended category order. I confirm no extra "anything else" category is needed since nothing beyond speakers exists, and the Drums Comp duplicate sends are properly applied to every drum channel alongside the main Drums bus, matching the stated provenance.

On the compressor notes for "No Stressor" at -20dB threshold with 20ms attack and 50ms release, since the schema lacks dedicated dynamics fields for Drums Comp, storing this as text notes seems acceptable rather than a real omission. Checking patch stated flags, MON1-4 being marked true as explicit destinations aligns with the convention of defaulting to local XLR outputs 1-4 unless otherwise spe…

Matrix1 also correctly shows stated true per the convention for internal XLRs 7 and 8, gain_db defaults of 20 hold for guitars/keys/horns/strings/vocals, and trim values of 0 with head-amp are all consistent. The Snare Verb bus feeding only from Snare checks out since no other snare channels exist, unassigned_inputs is correctly empty, and DCA indexing for the Tracks bus matches actual assignment…

I'm also confirming the FX mute group and DCA correctly include all effects return busses, and that INST Reverb sends are properly applied post-fader across all instrument channels (guitars, keys, horns, strings, bass) while correctly excluding drums and tracks per convention.

Checking BassDI's DCA "Band" and mute group assignment confirms good. Now I'm verifying the Drums Comp duplicate bus's channel membership, checking whether Pads, PERC1, PERC2 alongside the core drum channels (Kick, Snare, HiHat, Toms, overheads) all correctly send to both Drums and Drums Comp busses.

Both bus sends check out consistently. Now I'm cross-referencing the patching convention order — drums, bass, guitars, keys, strings/brass, vocals, tracks, then speakers, then everything else — and noticing that speakers (HOST, ch30) are placed before tracks (ch31-38), which violates this order and is worth flagging as a warning. I'm also confirming the Tracks/Playback color is correctly Yellow, …

I'm also checking that no declared DCAs, mute groups, or MON buses are left unused — everything appears to be actively referenced. The ordering convention quote matches verbatim in the conventions text, so I'll finalize the output with that single finding: an intent-type violation for the speaker/track ordering, marked as a warning severity.
